paper_title: Bounding Helly Numbers via Betti Numbers
statement: 1 By definition, a homology cell is a topological space X all of whose (reduced, singular, integer coefficient) homology groups are trivial, as is the case if X = Rd or X is a single point. Here and in what follows, we refer the reader to standard textbooks like [12, 22] for further topological background and various topological notions that we leave undefined. 2 An open good cover is a finite family of open subsets of Rd such that the intersection of any sub-family of at most d members is either empty or is contractible (and hence, in particular, a homology cell). 3 We recall that a topological space X is k-connected, for some integer k ≥ 0, if every continuous map S i → X from the i-dimensional sphere to X, 0 ≤ i ≤ k, can be extended to a map Di+1 → X from the (i + 1)-dimensional disk to X. 4 We also remark that our condition can be verified algorithmically since Betti numbers are easily computable, at least for sufficiently nice spaces that can be represented by finite simplicial complexes, say. By contrast, it is algorithmically undecidable whether a given 2-dimensional simplicial complex is 1-connected, see, e.g., the survey [26].
